**Needs changes before merge.**

Safety-floor review. The shipped post script decides the posted G-code, so the folder lookup is the main subject of this review.

### What looks good

- The posted output with the shipped files is the same as on `main`. No file under `tests/golden/` changes, and all golden suites pass (table below).
- A missing directory, a missing file, a file that is not UTF-8 and a file over 4 MiB each give an `Err` that names the file and the directory. There is no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` on these paths. There is no silent fallback to a different script on the desktop.
- One directory is used for each kind. Files are never mixed from two directories.
- Each file is read one time for each process (`OnceLock` cells in `posting_files.rs`). An edit during a run cannot give half-old and half-new output. The module doc and the decision file say this.
- Each read writes the full path to the log at `info`. `info` is in `logging::DEFAULT_FILTER`, so the line is written by default.
- The `wasm32` list agrees with the tables. I compared them: the 16 posts, the 43 machines and `3axis-vmc.mch` (60 entries) are all in `embedded()`. Each `.cps` and `.mch` file in `assets/` is in a table.
- Packaging. Each package puts `assets/posts` and `assets/machines` where candidate 1 or 2 finds them:
  - Windows zip and Inno installer: `ASSET_DIRS` in `xtask/src/release_pack.rs`, then the installer copies the whole stage.
  - Linux tarball, deb and rpm: `/usr/lib/camcraft/assets`. The `/usr/bin` wrapper uses `exec`, so `current_exe` is in `/usr/lib/camcraft`.
  - AppImage: `usr/bin/assets`.
  - macOS bundle: `Contents/Resources/assets`.
  - FreeBSD: `assets` beside the binaries.
  - Snap and flatpak: built from the Linux tarball (`/app/bin/assets` for flatpak).
  - AUR: `/usr/lib/camcraft/assets`.
- No new crate edge. `posting_files.rs` (301 lines) and `data_dir.rs` (163 lines) are below 400 lines. The PR body has the `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #2282`. The decision file is present.

### Results (merged with `main` 3701b32d8, built locally)

The trial merge had no conflicts.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-post` lib (9 new `data_dir` tests) | 74 passed |
| `camcraft-app` lib | 357 passed, 1 ignored |
| `shipped_from_disk` (new) | 3 passed |
| `posting` / `machine` / `machine_library` | 17 / 33 / 11 passed |
| `post_serves_kind` / `post_serves_plasma` | 6 / 1 passed |
| `golden_cl` / `conformance` / `solid_law_goldens` | 33 / 7 / 7 passed |
| `tormach_post` / `tormach_machines` / `tinyg_post` / `grblhal_post` | 10 / 6 / 18 / 9 passed |
| `carvera_post` / `altmill_machines` / `haas_machines` | 4 / 4 / 3 passed |
| `plasma_post` / `plasma_post_refusals` | 5 / 7 passed |
| `program_units` / `program_comments` / `post_cycle_feed_spindle` / `lathe_post_inch` | 7 / 4 / 8 / 6 passed |
| `wire_post` / `sodick_wire_post` / `sodick_alc400g` / `sinker_burn` | 12 / 9 / 5 / 15 passed |
| `smoothing` / `explain_option` / `setup_mount_trace` / `machine_assign` / `machine_edit` | 7 / 4 / 6 / 3 / 12 passed |

| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean, except the `main` error below |

All `camcraft-app` test binaries compile (`--keep-going`), except one. That one is broken on `main` itself and is not caused by this PR (#2297):

```
error[E0063]: missing field `body` in initializer of `camcraft_app::fixture_locate::LocateSpec`
   --> crates\app\tests\stock_in_vise_sim.rs:103:16
```

### Requested before merge

1. **The per-user folder can replace the repository scripts with no warning.** `crates/post/src/data_dir.rs:65-73` puts candidate 3 (`<user data>/camcraft/assets/<kind>`) before candidate 4 (dev run) and candidate 5 (source tree). A `cargo run` exe and each test binary in `target/*/deps/` do not find candidate 1. If `%APPDATA%\camcraft\assets\posts` (or `~/.local/share/camcraft/assets/posts`) exists on a machine, they read that copy and not the repository files. Then the golden suites test a different script on that one machine, and the only trace is an `info` line. The per-user folder also never wins for an intact package, because candidate 1 or 2 always exists there. Thus it gives no user override, only a place for a stale copy. Do one of these:
   - remove candidate 3 (the decision already drops per-file user overrides, and #2282 does not ask for a user copy); or
   - put candidate 3 after candidates 4 and 5, and log the resolved directory at `warn` when it is not candidate 1 or 2.

   Change `the_order_is_exe_user_dev_manifest` (`data_dir_tests.rs`) to agree.
2. **A release exe can read the build machine's checkout.** `data_dir.rs:118` puts `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` into every binary, the release exe included. On the machine that built the release (the maintainer's checkout, a self-hosted runner), a package with no `assets/` folder reads the posts of the branch that is checked out at that time. Candidate 4 has a similar problem: `<exe dir>/../../assets` is `/usr/assets` for `/usr/lib/camcraft/camcraft-ui` and `C:\assets` for `C:\Program Files\CamCraft\camcraft-ui.exe`. Use candidates 4 and 5 only when the exe is in a cargo target tree: the exe directory is `target/<profile>` or `target/<profile>/deps`. Do not use `cfg(debug_assertions)`, because the release-tier lanes run test binaries in release. Add a test: an installed-layout exe path gives only candidates 1-3.

### Questions and notes (not blocking)

- The `Changelog:` line says "an edit there takes effect without a rebuild". Because the read is one time for each process, the edit takes effect at the next start. Please add "after a restart" so that a user does not expect a live reload.
- `DataFiles::read` and its `Mutex<HashMap>` cache are not used by the app: `posting_files.rs` calls `read_file` and caches in its own cells. The test `an_edited_file_on_disk_is_what_loads_and_the_read_is_cached` therefore pins a cache that production does not use. Use `DataFiles::read` in `posting_files.rs`, or remove the unused cache and move the pin to `posting_files`.
- No test pins the 4 MiB refusal (`MAX_BYTES`). A small test with a cap parameter, or a sparse file, would pin it.
- No test pins the `embedded()` list against `BUILTINS`/`MACHINES`. I compared them by hand, and they agree today. Open PRs that add posts (#2290, #2253, #2162) can easily miss the `wasm32` arm. A `cfg(any(target_arch = "wasm32", test))` on `embedded` and a test that walks the tables would catch this.
- Posts and machines resolve independently, so they can come from two different folders. With item 1 or 2 fixed this is unlikely. A one-time log line for each kind that names the resolved directory would make it visible.
- `crates/app/tests/import_step_guard.rs` and `import_step_guard_default_cap.rs` change only in line endings (214 lines, empty with `git diff -w --ignore-cr-at-eol`). This is not related to #2282. Please drop it.
- `PostRef::Builtin` keeps its meaning (entry 0, Fanuc), and the project file does not change. No format bump is necessary.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: f5ce379c15428c7fe09ce5b5b1569c4305cd9180 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Re-review of the delta `30a81b012..f5ce379c1` (one commit). Safety-floor tier, because the shipped post script decides the posted G-code.

### The two earlier blockers

1. **Per-user folder: removed.** `crates/post/src/data_dir.rs` has no user-data candidate and no environment read. The only lookup inputs are `current_exe()` and `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`. Nothing else can shadow the shipped files: the first candidate that exists wins for the whole kind, and on an installed exe the only candidates are `<exe dir>/assets/<kind>` and the macOS bundle `Resources`.
2. **Dev fallbacks only in a cargo build tree: correct.** `cargo_profile_dir` (`data_dir.rs:44-50`) accepts the exe folder, or the folder above `deps` / `examples`, only when it holds `.fingerprint`. I tried these layouts:
   - deb/rpm `/usr/lib/camcraft`, the Windows installer and zip, AppImage `usr/bin`, flatpak `/app/bin`, snap: no `.fingerprint`, so one candidate. A missing `assets` folder gives the named refusal. `/usr/assets`, `C:\assets` and the build machine's checkout are never read.
   - macOS bundle: `Contents/MacOS` gives candidates 1 and 2 only.
   - Symlinked exe: Linux `current_exe` gives the resolved target. On macOS it can give the link folder (for example `/usr/local/bin`). That folder has no `assets` and no `.fingerprint`, so the result is the named refusal, not a wrong script.
   - `cargo install` into `~/.cargo/bin`: cargo builds in a temporary target and copies only the binary. There is no `.fingerprint`, so the result is the named refusal. That is acceptable, because `cargo install` is not a shipped layout.
   - A user folder that holds a `.fingerprint` folder: candidate 1 still comes first. The fallbacks apply only when that folder also has no `assets/<kind>`. In that case `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` is a path of the build machine and does not exist on the user's machine. This case is contrived and is not blocking.
   - `cargo run` (`target/<profile>`), `cargo test` (`target/<profile>/deps`) and the release-tier test binaries in `target/release/deps` find the repository `assets`. The `cargo xtask release` stage puts `assets/` beside the exe, so candidate 1 wins.
   - Panics: there is none. `cargo_profile_dir` uses `?` on `parent()`, `candidates` does no indexing, and `resolve` returns `Err`.

### What looks good

- The two `import_step_guard` files are no longer in the PR diff against `main`. The delta restores them; it is empty with `-w --ignore-cr-at-eol`.
- The new tests pin what they claim:
  - `an_installed_exe_without_assets_is_refused_not_redirected`: on the old head, `/usr/assets/posts` would resolve, so this test would fail there.
  - `the_order_is_exe_dev_manifest_in_a_cargo_tree`: the `deps` case fails if the `deps` / `examples` arm is removed.
  - `a_file_over_the_size_cap_is_refused_by_name`: pins the 4 MiB refusal at `MAX_BYTES` and `MAX_BYTES + 1`.
  - `the_browser_list_matches_the_disk_tables`: walks `BUILTINS`, `MACHINES` and the default machine against `embedded()`.
- The `Changelog:` line now says "after a restart". The decision file records the dropped per-user folder and the dropped `cfg(debug_assertions)` option.
- No process files, no `build.rs`, no `Cargo.toml` change. No new crate edge.

### Results (merged with `main` e8c0eb63d, built locally)

The trial merge had no conflicts (`crates/app/src/posting.rs` auto-merged).

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib` | 75 passed |
| `camcraft-app --test shipped_from_disk` | 3 passed |
| `--test posting` / `--test machine` / `--test machine_library` | 17 / 33 / 11 passed |
| `--test golden_cl` / `--test tormach_post` | 33 / 10 passed |
| `camcraft-app` lib `the_browser_list_matches_the_disk_tables` | 1 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

All runs used `-j 6` and `--test-threads=6`.

### Requested before merge

None.

### Questions and notes (not blocking)

- Candidate 3 (`<profile>/../../assets`) is computed from depth only. With a target folder outside the repository (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/x/cargo-target`), it points to `C:/Users/x/assets/<kind>`. That folder comes before candidate 4 (the source tree). This affects only dev and test runs, and an `assets/posts` folder at that place is unlikely. In a cargo tree, candidate 4 always names the source tree of the same build. Thus candidate 3 adds no case that candidate 4 does not cover. You can remove candidate 3, or accept it only when `<repo>/Cargo.toml` exists. The decision file says that the marker "works with a custom `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`". That is true for the marker, but not for candidate 3.
- With `--target <triple>`, candidate 3 is `target/assets` and is not found. Candidate 4 then wins, so the result is correct.
- From the earlier review, still open by choice: the `DataFiles::read` cache is not used by `posting_files.rs`, and there is no one-time log line for each kind that names the resolved directory. Each read already logs its full path at `info`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
